parties.respondent_defendant: Renukappa, husband of Gangawwa, and others

facts_of_case: The parties are Gangawwa and Renukappa Burli, who were accused of bigamy punishable under Section 494 of IPC read with Section 17 A of The Hindu Marriage Act. The trial court acquitted the respondents.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the complainant to prove the second marriage.
legal_principles.held: Learned Judge having heard the arguments and appreciating the evidence on record, has yielded that, complainant has failed to prove that accused persons have married Smt. Laxmavva, the accused and thereby committed an offence under Section 494 of IPC.

legal_principles.principle: The court's findings are based on the appreciation of evidence and not just the arguments.
legal_principles.held: Learned Judge having heard the arguments and appreciating the evidence on record, has yielded that, complainant has failed to prove that accused persons have married Smt. Laxmavva, the accused and thereby committed an offence under Section 494 of IPC.
use_in: all cases where evidence is crucial

outcome.final_order: The appeal was dismissed and the judgment dated 24.5.2003 passed by the trial court was upheld.
